chunks: From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about the charity (sadaqah) of a young boy who has not yet reached puberty (ihtilam). He said, 'Yes, if he places it in the place designated for charity.'

key_terms.يَحْتَلِم: To reach puberty (specifically via nocturnal emission)

ai.seo_question: Is the charity of a young child who has not yet reached puberty considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the charity of a pre-pubescent child (*ghulam*) is legally valid, contingent upon the funds being designated in a proper charitable context. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that minors possess independent financial capacity for voluntary acts of worship, provided their guardians ensure the correct allocation of assets, reflecting the broader principle of *ahl al-ghina* (those capable of holding wealth) extending to children in specific legal contexts.
